data.narrative:
Meter is a Series C-stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Anil and Sunil Varanasi. The analysis draws on a limited comp universe comprising one private peer (ICON) and no public comparables, reflecting the early-stage nature of frontier construction technology. This scarcity of direct peers constrains the reliability of market-based triangulation.

The valuation exercise relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to Meter's $305M total capital raised proxy. This approach yields an implied valuation of $518M. The methodology assumes that future funding rounds will command premium multiples consistent with demonstrated traction and market validation at the Series C stage, though this carries execution risk inherent to early-stage ventures.

The triangulated range spans $441M (low) to $596M (high), with a median of $518M. The relatively narrow band reflects methodological consistency rather than analytical depth; the single-method foundation and sparse comp coverage mean this range should be treated as indicative rather than definitive. Key uncertainties include unit economics validation in housing applications, path to profitability, and whether frontier construction tech multiples will sustain through later rounds. Additional data on revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and burn dynamics would materially strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this range.
